{
  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(
    input [7:0] address,
    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,
    input [7:0] b,
    input control,
    output [15:0] count
);
    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;

    wire [7:0] residue1, residue2;
    wire [15:0] count1, count2;

    assign residue1 = ptr1 - base;
    assign residue2 = ptr2 - base;

    addr_calcu_sum lane1(address, b, residue1, count1);
    addr_calcu_sum lane2(address, b, residue2, count2);

    assign count = (control == 1'b1) ? count1 : count2;
endmodule

module addr_calcu_sum(
    input [7:0] a,
    input [7:0] b,
    input [7:0] r,
    output [15:0] result
);
    wire [7:0] ab_xor;
    wire [7:0] s, majority;
    wire [7:1] p, g;
    wire [8:1] carry;
    wire [7:0] low;
    wire upper0, upper1;
    wire nonzero, negative;

    // Carry-save representation of the three unsigned operands.
    assign ab_xor = a ^ b;
    assign s = ab_xor ^ r;
    assign majority = (a & b) | (ab_xor & r);

    // Add s and (majority << 1), retaining both upper bits.
    assign p = s[7:1] ^ majority[6:0];
    assign g = s[7:1] & majority[6:0];
    assign carry[1] = 1'b0;
    assign carry[2] = g[1];
    assign carry[3] = g[2] | (p[2] & g[1]);
    assign carry[4] = g[3] | (p[3] & g[2])
                    | (p[3] & p[2] & g[1]);
    assign carry[5] = g[4] | (p[4] & carry[4]);
    assign carry[6] = g[5] | (p[5] & g[4])
                    | (p[5] & p[4] & carry[4]);
    assign carry[7] = g[6] | (p[6] & g[5])
                    | (p[6] & p[5] & g[4])
                    | (p[6] & p[5] & p[4] & carry[4]);
    assign carry[8] = g[7] | (p[7] & g[6])
                    | (p[7] & p[6] & g[5])
                    | (p[7] & p[6] & p[5] & g[4])
                    | (p[7] & p[6] & p[5] & p[4] & carry[4]);

    assign low[0] = s[0];
    assign low[7:1] = p ^ carry[7:1];
    assign upper0 = majority[7] ^ carry[8];
    assign upper1 = majority[7] & carry[8];

    // Subtract 256 exactly when the modular residue is nonzero.
    assign nonzero = |r;
    assign negative = nonzero & ~upper1 & ~upper0;
    assign result = {{7{negative}}, (upper0 ^ nonzero), low};
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The original data paths serialize an 8-bit modular subtraction, a 16-bit subtraction, and a 16-bit addition before the final control mux. Upper-byte arithmetic is largely redundant but can contribute carry-chain delay.",
  "rewrite": "Use r = (ptr - base) modulo 256. The original result is address + b + r - (r != 0 ? 256 : 0), modulo 65536. At base=128, forming r only complements the pointer MSB. Each parallel lane uses carry-save compression and grouped carry lookahead for the low-byte sum, then reconstructs the upper byte from two carry bits and the nonzero-residue flag. The output mux remains after both arithmetic lanes.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to reduce maximum arrival by eliminating the offset-subtraction chain and full-width cascaded arithmetic. The late control still traverses only the final mux. No numerical timing improvement is claimed without running the specified mapping flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Two arithmetic lanes are retained for control-path timing. Common address/b XOR and AND terms can merge during flattening and synthesis. Grouped lookahead adds parallel carry logic, while removal of wide arithmetic should offset its cost. Compliance with the area cap and zero electrical violations requires mapped evaluation; neither has been measured here.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module interface, unsigned widths, 8-bit base parameter, modular pointer arithmetic, 16-bit result, and control selection for every two-state input. The actual lane result ranges from -255 through 510, so bits 15:9 are exactly the replicated negative flag. The residue-zero case is handled separately, including ptr=base. The algebra also holds for other 8-bit base overrides. Entirely combinational Verilog-2001 with no storage or external dependencies."
}
